title: Capacity split simulation playbook and operator cheat sheet
author: Asha Patel
body:
Overview:

This playbook defines a repeatable, low-risk process to run capacity-split simulations for Redwood’s multi-tenant inference platform and provides a compact operator cheat sheet for executing and remediating experiments. The goal is to validate: autoscaler behavior, tenant split performance, cross-region routing, and SLO preservation under controlled capacity fragmentation scenarios.

Intended audience:
- Platform operators
- Capacity planners
- Oncall engineers running live experiments
- SREs validating degradation/runback strategies

Goals:
- Verify that the autoscaler and priority-tenant logic maintain p99 latency SLOs within budget when capacity is split across regions/pools.
- Surface regressions in KV-prefix cache hit-rate, batching efficiency, and queue saturation.
- Validate operator rollback and tenant merge procedures with <30m customer-impact window.

Scope and safety:
- This playbook targets non-production synthetic tenants and a select set of canary customers (explicit consent required).
- All simulations must run in the designated simulation region (sim-1) or enabled staging accounts unless explicitly approved by Product Ops.
- Abort window: Any sustained SLO burn >20% for >10m triggers immediate safe-stop (see abort procedure).

Ownership:
- Run owner: oncall platform operator (primary)
- Validation owner: capacity-planning (secondary)
- Stakeholder notifications: product infra, customer success (if canary customers involved)

Pre-simulation checklist (must be green):
- [ ] Simulation fleet health: all nodes in sim clusters show Ready and have thermal budget >= 20%.
- [ ] Dashboards deployed: "Platform / Simulation / Capacity Split" and "Platform / Token Latency" visible to run owner.
- [ ] Canary set defined: tenant IDs and cardinality verified in the simulation manifest.
- [ ] Rollback runbook loaded to operator clipboard (commands below).
- [ ] Incident channel created: #ops-simulations-<YYYYMMDD>-<run-id>.

Configuration artifacts:
- Simulation manifest (example):

```yaml
run_id: split-sim-20260203-01
duration: 30m
tenants: 1200
profiles:
  - name: small-embed
    qps: 0.2
    model: eco-embed-1
  - name: chat-burst
    qps: 1.0
    model: rdx-chat-2
split_policy:
  - region_a: sim-1 (60% weight)
  - region_b: sim-2 (40% weight)
safeties:
  abort_slo_burn_pct: 20
  abort_window_minutes: 10
```

Simulation orchestration commands (platform-simctl):
- Start: platform-simctl start --manifest=manifests/split-sim-20260203-01.yaml --dry-run=false --notes="operator:asha"
- Pause: platform-simctl pause --run=split-sim-20260203-01
- Resume: platform-simctl resume --run=split-sim-20260203-01
- Force-stop (safe-stop): platform-simctl stop --run=split-sim-20260203-01 --graceful=true

Operator quick-checks (first 5m):
1) Verify request distribution: query the simulation summary endpoint: curl -s https://sim-control.internal/runs/split-sim-20260203-01/summary | jq
2) Confirm p95/p99 token latency is within expected band: p95 < 120ms, p99 < 420ms (simulation tolerance).
3) Spot-check kernel selection rates: dashboard tile "Kernel switch rate" should not exceed 8% per-minute.

Primary simulation steps (detailed):
1. Preflight (T-60m):
   - Announce run in #ops-simulations and schedule a 60m monitoring window with key stakeholders.
   - Snapshot autoscaler config and current pool allocations: kubectl -n platform get configmap autoscaler-config -o yaml > /tmp/autoscaler-config.pre.yaml
   - Create snapshot of telemetry retention and sampling rates.
2. Inject synthetic load (T+0):
   - Start small cohort (10% of tenants) for 10m to validate routing and cache warmup.
   - Expand to target cardinality incrementally (10% steps every 5m) until full load.
3. Stabilize (mid-run):
   - Observe batching efficiency and KV hit-rate. If KV hit-rate drops >15% from baseline for >8m: enable prefetch hint for affected prefixes (operator UI > Prefetch -> "enable-hints") or run prefetch script: platform-prefetchctl --cohort=split-sim-20260203-01 --enable
4. De-escalation (T+duration - 10m):
   - Stop new tenant injections and observe tail-latency recovery.
5. Post-run snapshot:
   - Export runtime metrics, tracing spans, and autoscaler decisions to the run archive.

Failure scenarios, detection, and mitigations (condensed table):

| Scenario | Detection signal | Immediate mitigation | Owner |
|---------|------------------|----------------------|-------|
| Autoscaler overshoot (throttled queues) | Queue length > 1500 reqs for 5m; token-burn spike | Pause simulator injection; reduce split weight to region_a by 20% | platform operator |
| KV-prefix cache collapse | KV hit-rate drop >20% and burst of remote fetch traces | Enable per-prefix prefetch; temporarily increase cache retention by 2x | runtime team |
| Model variant fallback storm | >3% of requests invoking fallback model per-minute | Force model pin for canary tenants to a stable variant, disable JIT kernel switching | serving-runtime |
| Thermal throttle (GPU) | Node thermal alarms or >90% GPU thermally constrained | Shift tenants to alternate pools; initiate safe-stop if >2 nodes affected | infra ops |

Observability and dashboards to watch:
- Platform / Simulation / Capacity Split (aggregate request distribution, run status)
- Platform / Token Latency (p50/p95/p99, per-tenant and per-profile breakdown)
- Runtime / KV Cache (hit-rate, cold fetch rate, prefix-level metrics)
- Autoscaler / Decisions (scale events, reasons, predicted vs actual)
- Hardware / GPU Thermal (per-node temperature, throttling events)

Alert thresholds (operator-facing):
- sim-run:token-p99:fire when p99 > 500ms for >5m (critical)
- sim-run:queue-length:warn when queue_length > 900 for >10m
- sim-run:kv-hit-drop:warn when kv_hit_rate drops >15% from baseline for >8m
- sim-run:autoscaler-oscillation:warn when >5 scale_up/scale_down cycles within 10m

Abort (safe-stop) procedure (immediate steps):
1) Run owner posts to #ops-simulations and calls the incident bridge.
2) platform-simctl stop --run=<run_id> --graceful=true (stop new injections, let in-flight finish within 60s).
3) If SLOs continue to burn after graceful stop, escalate to emergency rollback: platform-operator rollback-autoscaler --snapshot=/tmp/autoscaler-config.pre.yaml --force
4) Reallocate traffic away from simulation region: routingctl set-weight sim-1=0 --reason="abort-<run_id>"

Post-simulation analysis checklist:
- Archive run artifacts: metrics, traces, simulation manifest, autoscaler logs. Location: s3://redwood-sim-archives/<run_id>
- Run the regression detector: sim-analysis --run <run_id> --baseline <last-good-run> --report out/<run_id>-comparison.html
- Fill the quick retro: root_cause, detection_time, mitigation_effectiveness, operator_notes.

Retro template (to paste into a page):
- Run ID: 
- Run owner: 
- Duration: 
- Observed regressions (metrics + evidence): 
- Primary cause (suspected): 
- Mitigation taken: 
- Time to mitigate: 
- Post-mortem required: yes/no
- Action items (owner + due date):

Operator cheat sheet (commands and snippets):
- Start simulation (full): platform-simctl start --manifest=manifests/split-sim.yaml --notes="operator:<you>"
- Quick status: platform-simctl status --run=<run_id>
- Snapshot autoscaler config: kubectl -n platform get cm autoscaler-config -o yaml > /tmp/autoscaler-config.pre.yaml
- Increase cache retention (temporary): runtimectl cache set-retention --multiplier=2 --prefix=sim-
- Safe-stop (fast): platform-simctl stop --run=<run_id> --graceful=false && routingctl set-weight sim-1=0

Known pitfalls and mitigation heuristics:
- Pitfall: starting full cardinality immediately leads to cold-cache thrash. Mitigation: ramp cohorts in 10% increments and validate KV hit-rate after each step.
- Pitfall: autoscaler hysteresis hides slow regressions. Mitigation: enable debug verbosity on autoscaler for the run and collect predicted decision deltas.

Metrics to export for post-analysis (minimum):
- p50/p95/p99 token latency (per-profile)
- token consumption per-tenant per-minute
- KV cache hit-rate by prefix and by cohort
- batching efficiency (tokens per batch, batches per-second)
- autoscaler scale events (timestamped decisions)

Change and rollout notes after a successful run:
- If the experiment uncovers a safe improvement (e.g., prefetch hint reduces p99 by >10% without cost increase), create a change proposal and schedule a staged rollout using the canary flow in /confluence/eng-platform/how-tos/canary-orchestration-dsl-and-safe-rollback-playbook-2026.

Appendix: Example simulation post-run command sequence
- platform-simctl export --run=split-sim-20260203-01 --dest=s3://redwood-sim-archives/split-sim-20260203-01
- sim-analysis --run split-sim-20260203-01 --baseline split-sim-20251201-01 --out reports/split-sim-20260203-01.html

FAQ (short):
Q: Can we run this against production tenant traffic?
A: No. Production runs require an explicit enterprise signoff and use special traffic shadowing that mirrors live traffic but does not affect customer request paths. See eng-private-deployments/onprem-packaging for additional constraints.

Q: How long should a standard simulation run?
A: Typical runs are 30m to 90m depending on scope. Longer runs (>2h) are reserved for capacity regression windows and require escalated approvals.

Related pages and references:
- Platform autoscaler design doc: /confluence/eng-platform/systems-and-services/predictive-batching-routing-roadmap-2026 (for background heuristics)
- Runbook: regional-capacity-thaw-freeze-and-conservation-runbook-2026 (for thaw/freeze safety)

Contact and escalation:
- Primary: oncall-platform@redwood (pager)
- Capacity planning: capacity-planning@redwood
- Runtime team pager: runtime-sre@redwood
